title: 1995 AMC 8 Problem 23
statement: How many four-digit whole numbers are there such that the leftmost digit is odd, the second digit is even, and all four digits are different?

solutions.text:
The first digit is odd: \(5\) choices. The second is even: \(5\) choices (none of which repeats the odd first digit).

The third digit is any of the \(8\) unused digits, and the fourth is any of the \(7\) remaining. In total, \(5 \times 5 \times 8 \times 7 = 1400.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B .
hints: Count choices for each digit position in turn: first, second, third, fourth
First digit: \(5\) odd options; second: \(5\) even options; then \(8\) and \(7\) for the distinct remaining digits
